items.title: Section: The Fire-Drilling Simile — Warmth, Summit, Forbearance, and the Supreme Worldly Dharma

items.zh: 即由如是諸根、諸力，漸修、漸習、漸多修習為因緣故，便能發起下中上品順決擇分四種善根。何等為四？一、煗，二、頂，三、順諦忍，四、世第一法。譬如有人，欲以其火作火所作，為求火故，下安乾木，上施鑽燧，精勤、策勵、勇猛鑽求。彼於如是精勤、策勵、勇猛鑽時，於下木上最初生煗；次煗增長，熱氣上衝；次倍增盛，其煙遂發；次無焰火欻然流出；火出無間發生猛焰；猛焰生已，便能造作火之所作。
items.en: Through gradual practice, gradual habituation, and gradual thorough cultivation of these very faculties and powers as cause and condition, one gives rise to the lower, middle, and upper grades of the four roots of goodness conducive to penetration: warmth, summit, forbearance in according with the truths, and the supreme worldly dharma. It is like a person wishing to produce fire and make use of it — laying dry wood below, applying the drill above, diligently, vigorously, courageously drilling in pursuit of fire: warmth first arises upon the wood below; next the warmth increases, and heat rises; next it redoubles, and smoke appears; next flameless fire suddenly issues forth; the fire, without interruption, gives rise to a fierce blaze; and once that fierce blaze has arisen, it becomes able to do fire's own work.

items.zh: 如鑽火人精勤、策勵、勇猛鑽求，五根、五力，漸修、漸習、漸多修習，當知亦爾。如下木上初所生煗，其煗善根，當知亦爾，燒諸煩惱無漏法火生前相故。如煗增長，熱氣上衝，其頂善根，當知亦爾。如次煙發，其順諦忍，當知亦爾。如無焰火欻然流出，世第一法，當知亦爾。如火無間發生猛焰，世第一法所攝五根、五力，無間所生出世無漏聖法，當知亦爾。

items.title: Section: The Seven Factors of Enlightenment Open

items.zh: 此復云何？謂七覺支。諸已證入正性離生補特伽羅如實覺慧用此為支，故名覺支。
items.en: What follows this? The seven factors of enlightenment. Those beings who have already entered the true nature that departs from arising make use of these as the very supports of their truly awakened wisdom — this is why they are called factors of enlightenment.

items.title: Section: The Seven Factors Sorted by Calm and Insight; the Eightfold Path Opens

items.zh: 即此七種如實覺支，三品所攝。謂三覺支奢摩他品攝，三覺支毘鉢舍那品攝，一覺支通二品攝，是故說名七種覺支。謂擇法覺支、精進覺支、喜覺支，此三觀品所攝；安覺支、定覺支、捨覺支，此三止品所攝；念覺支一種，俱品所攝，說名遍行。彼於爾時，最初獲得七覺支故，名初有學見聖諦迹。已永斷滅見道所斷一切煩惱，唯餘修道所斷煩惱。為斷彼故，修習三蘊所攝八支聖道。此中正見、正思惟、正精進，慧蘊所攝；正語、正業、正命，戒蘊所攝；正念、正定，定蘊所攝。問：何因緣故名八支聖道？答：諸聖有學已見迹者，由八支攝行迹正道，能無餘斷一切煩惱，能於解脫究竟作證，是故名為八支聖道。
items.en: These same seven factors of true realisation are comprised within three categories: three factors belong to the calm-abiding category, three belong to the insight category, and one factor belongs to both categories — this is why they are called the seven factors of enlightenment. Investigation of phenomena, diligence, and joy belong to the insight category; pliancy, concentration, and equanimity belong to the calm-abiding category; mindfulness alone belongs to both, and is called pervasive. At that time, having just attained the seven factors of enlightenment, one is called a trainee who has newly seen the trace of the noble truths. Having permanently ended everything abandoned at the path of seeing, only what remains to be abandoned at the path of cultivation is left; in order to end this, one cultivates the eightfold noble path, comprised within the three aggregates.

items.zh: 當知此中，若覺支時所得真覺；若得彼已，以慧安立如證而覺，總略此二合名正見。由此正見增上力故，所起出離、無恚、無害分別思惟，名正思惟。
items.en: Know that here, the true realisation attained at the time of the seven factors, together with the wisdom that, once that realisation is attained, establishes it in words matching what has been directly witnessed — these two together are called right view. Through the power of this right view, the resulting deliberation marked by renunciation, freedom from ill will, and freedom from harm is called right intention.

items.zh: 若心趣入諸所尋思，彼唯尋思如是相狀所有尋思。若心趣入諸所言論，即由正見增上力故，起善思惟，發起種種如法言論，是名正語。若如法求衣服、飲食、諸坐臥具、病緣醫藥供身什物。於追求時，若往、若還正知而住，若覩、若瞻、若屈、若伸、若持衣鉢及僧伽胝、若食、若飲、若噉、若甞正知而住；或於住時，於已追求衣服等事，若行、若住、若坐、若臥，廣說乃至若解勞睡正知而住。是名正業。如法追求衣服、飲食，乃至什物，遠離一切起邪命法，是名正命。若遠離攝正語、業、命，彼於證得無漏作意諸覺支時，先已獲得。問：

blocks.text: How the faculties and powers lead up to the breakthrough, through a famous simile; then the seven factors of awakening. Two short passages (0444c20, 0445a19) are untranslated.

Through gradual practice of the faculties and powers, one gives rise to the four stages of preparation: **warmth, summit, forbearance in accord with the truths, and the highest worldly dharma**. The untranslated simile (0444c20): like someone drilling for fire, working hard and steadily. The first warmth in the lower wood is **warmth**, the sign before the uncontaminated fire that burns afflictions; the heat rising upwards is the **summit**; the smoke is **forbearance**; the first flameless fire suddenly flowing out is the **highest worldly dharma**; and the blazing flame that follows without interval is the supramundane noble path. Master Cháng Bǎi explains each stage.

"Those who have entered the true nature that departs from arising use these as the supports of their realisation": mindfulness, investigation of phenomena, effort, joy, pliancy, concentration, equanimity.

"Investigation, effort, and joy belong to the insight category; pliancy, concentration, and equanimity to calm; mindfulness alone belongs to both, and is called pervasive." Venerable Miào Jìng: mindfulness has room to work in both. "At that time, having just attained the seven factors, one is called a trainee who has newly seen the track."

"The true realisation attained at the time of the seven factors, together with the wisdom that establishes it in words": right view. "Through its power, the resulting deliberation marked by renunciation, freedom from ill will, and harmlessness": right intention.

quiz.q: What are the four roots of goodness conducive to penetration, and how does Master Cháng Bǎi map them to three grades?
options: warmth and summit lower, forbearance middle, supreme worldly dharma upper
quiz.why: "Warmth, summit, forbearance in according with the truths, and the supreme worldly dharma." Master Cháng Bǎi: warmth and summit may be called lower grade, forbearance middle, the supreme worldly dharma upper.

quiz.q: This treatise says the four roots arise from the faculties and powers. How do other treatises, as cited in the lectures, map them?
options: Cháng Bǎi cites the Kośa: right efforts warmth, bases summit, faculties forbearance, powers supreme; Miào Jìng cites the Abhidharmasamuccaya: warmth and summit faculties, forbearance and supreme powers
quiz.why: "Through gradual practice of these very faculties and powers as cause and condition, one gives rise to the lower, middle, and upper grades of the four roots of goodness." Master Cháng Bǎi: the Kośa maps right efforts to warmth, bases of power to summit, faculties to forbearance, powers to the supreme worldly dharma. Venerable Miào Jìng: that text (the Abhidharmasamuccaya) says warmth and summit are the faculties, forbearance and supreme are the powers.

quiz.q: Why are they called factors of enlightenment, and how does Master Cháng Bǎi explain "factor"?
options: those who have entered the path use these as supports of awakened wisdom; 支 means cause
quiz.why: "Those beings who have already entered the true nature that departs from arising make use of these as the very supports of their truly awakened wisdom." Master Cháng Bǎi: 支 means cause — these are seven causes of awakening, methods of awakening to the path.

quiz.q: Joy belongs to the insight category. What does Venerable Miào Jìng compare it to?
options: the first bodhisattva ground, the Joyful — same nature
quiz.why: "Investigation of phenomena, diligence, and joy belong to the insight category." Venerable Miào Jìng: in the Mahāyāna ten grounds, the first is the Joyful Ground — the same kind of joy.

quiz.q: Mindfulness "belongs to both categories and is called pervasive." What do the masters say?
options: both: mindfulness operates in calm and in insight; both need it
quiz.why: "Mindfulness alone belongs to both, and is called pervasive." Venerable Miào Jìng: mindfulness has room to work in calm and in insight, so this mental factor is broader. Master Cháng Bǎi: both calm and insight require mindfulness — it pervades both.

quiz.q: On first attaining the seven factors one "has newly seen the trace of the noble truths." How does Venerable Miào Jìng explain 跡?
options: 跡 is a road — the seven factors are the road to seeing the truths
quiz.why: "At that time, having just attained the seven factors of enlightenment, one is called a trainee who has newly seen the trace of the noble truths." Venerable Miào Jìng: 跡 is a road; the seven factors are the road to seeing the noble truths.

quiz.q: Right view combines which two, according to Venerable Miào Jìng?
options: the true realisation of the factors and wisdom expressing it — fundamental and subsequent knowledge together
quiz.why: "The true realisation attained at the time of the seven factors, together with the wisdom that, once attained, establishes it in words matching what has been witnessed — these two together are called right view." Venerable Miào Jìng: right view is fundamental knowledge and subsequent knowledge combined.
